formNotes.Capitalized: token with its first letter capitalised (sentence start, proper noun)

notes: Reverse index only: alien surface -> English source word and written form. The dictionary in data/alien-words.json is a separate artefact and is not replaced by this one.
The source word list is the speech table, which is the set of words the alien language actually contains. A word outside it has no entry, and the UI must say so instead of inventing one.
The English localisation is NOT part of the default word list: it also contains the player's own journal entries, UI hints, item descriptions and generated proper names, which no alien ever speaks.
Generated by running the local NMS.exe core generator (0x140E795C0) in Unicorn; the words are computed at build time, never read from a file.

The three forms exist because the dialogue path at 0x140ED0349 hashes the token with its case intact, while the Language Records path at 0x140EC556C calls _strlwr first, so one English word has up to three alien words.
0x140ED03FC may additionally upper-case the first byte of the generated word at a sentence start; that is a display transform, so surface lookups here are case-insensitive.
0x140E8FFE0 still rewrites Autophage surfaces into the alien script for subtitles; this index stores the pre-substitution surface, matching data/alien-words.json.
Tokens are split on the byte set decoded from NMS.exe at 0x140ECFD06; apostrophe and hyphen stay inside a token.
Tokens longer than 16 bytes are skipped because the game's string hash only has a <=16-byte path.
Autophage English values containing Greek letters are skipped and counted per race, because the hash implements the ASCII path only and guessing would be wrong.
One Autophage speech row (Id MINING) carries Race None and uses model 3 rather than the Generic model; that single word is not in this index.
Atlas and Autophage both resolve to model 0, so their files are identical by construction. That equality is expected and doubles as a consistency check on the generator.
A surface may list several English sources: the mapping is near-injective over real English words but not provably unique, so every candidate is kept rather than picking one.
No game process, web source, or community dictionary is used.
